research_scope: Five full source-free mathematical reviews of fields, integral domains, associative rings, sigma-algebras and ideals; ten unassigned references.

amendments.review_rationale: Read field as nonzero commutative unital ring where every nonzero element has multiplicative inverse, tracking 0≠1 and unit condition.
amendments.reason: Rechecked original mathematical text, complete effective contextual reference set, and prior amendments; distinguish defining laws from reusable constructions without changing already resolved links.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative ring with multiplicative identity
references.matching_note: Consolidation of 'commutative ring with identity' with the previously identified unital commutative-ring missing candidate; multiplication commutativity and a specified identity are both required, unlike optional-unity associative ring.

references.disposition: Requiring 0≠1 excludes the zero ring and is part of the definition of a field, not a separate assumed mathematical structure.
The assertion that each nonzero a admits b with ab=ba=1 is the field's defining invertibility axiom, not a prerequisite equivalent to being a field.
Integral domains need not be fields; no alternative division-ring noncommutative context is assumed.
references.phrase: field requires all nonzero elements invertible

amendments.review_rationale: Read integral domain under commutative unital nonzero convention as no zero divisors, retaining 0≠1 and ring commutativity.
amendments.reason: Rechecked original mathematical text, complete effective contextual reference set, and prior amendments; distinguish defining laws from reusable constructions without changing already resolved links.

references.context: Ring theory: commutative associative ring R with two-sided unity 1_R and 0_R≠1_R, without an assumption that every nonzero element is invertible.
references.reason: The nonzero commutative unital ring is a reusable base structure, strictly weaker than an integral domain.

references.disposition: Condition ab=0⇒(a=0 or b=0) for all a,b is the zero-divisor exclusion axiom defining an integral domain, not a separate assumed property.
The zero ring is excluded in this integral-domain convention.

amendments.review_rationale: Read nonunital associative ring axioms: abelian additive group, associative multiplication and left/right distributivity, explicitly not requiring multiplicative identity.
amendments.reason: Rechecked original mathematical text, complete effective contextual reference set, and prior amendments; distinguish defining laws from reusable constructions without changing already resolved links.

references.disposition: Associativity (ab)c=a(bc) is one of the defining ring axioms, not a separately linked ring structure.
The left and right distributive laws over the abelian additive group are ring-defining axioms, not a distinct prerequisite for this ring.

references.phrase: unit is optional in this ring convention
references.disposition: Existence of 1 is not an axiom, unlike most unital commutative-algebra conventions.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed complete sigma-algebra axioms on an underlying set, recording power set, relative complement and countable union separately and distinguishing the positive-integer indexing convention.
amendments.reason: Rechecked original mathematical text, complete effective contextual reference set, and prior amendments; distinguish defining laws from reusable constructions without changing already resolved links.

references.context: Set theory: power set of an arbitrary underlying set X, namely the collection of all subsets of X; variable names X and S are interchangeable.
references.matching_note: Consolidated original notation 'power set P(X)' into the same set-theoretic power-set concept; no suitably typed meaning occurs among existing meanings.

references.context: Set theory: relative complement X\A={x∈X:x∉A}, where A⊆X; in a sigma-algebra it is applied to each measurable member A.
references.reason: Relative set complement is independently reusable; closure under it is a defining sigma-algebra axiom.

references.context: Set theory: countable union ⋃_{n≥1}A_n={x:there exists positive integer n with x∈A_n} of an indexed sequence of subsets of X.
references.reason: The countable union is a reusable set operation; closure of Σ under the operation is the defining condition.

references.disposition: The requirement X belongs to the family Sigma is an axiom of the definition, not a claim that Sigma contains every subset.

amendments.review_rationale: Reviewed two-sided ideal for a possibly noncommutative associative ring, retaining additive subgroup and both left/right multiplicative absorption as independent conditions.
amendments.reason: Rechecked original mathematical text, complete effective contextual reference set, and prior amendments; distinguish defining laws from reusable constructions without changing already resolved links.

references.matching_note: A subgroup of the ambient additive (abelian) group, satisfying the inherited group operation and inverse axioms; the generic subgroup definition is context-appropriate.

references.disposition: The universal condition rI⊆I is the left-side absorption axiom of a two-sided ideal; ring multiplication is already indexed.
The universal condition Ir⊆I is the right-side absorption axiom of a two-sided ideal, not an additional ring construction.
Both multiplication directions are required; commutativity is not assumed.
references.phrase: two-sided not merely left or right ideal
